approach: Root cause: a file kept by hand as a mirror of a governing source (xtask/shard-timings.txt, docs/decisions.md, status::BUILD_PATHS against the CI athena-bin key, docs/ontology.toml) is tested for its shape only, or checked late, so content that contradicts the source passes until the final verdict. Fix at the origin with one registry, crates/athena-core/src/mirrors.rs: each entry names a mirror file, its source and a comparison rule; pure rule functions compare content. Four rules: (a) shard-timings `--test` and `--lib` lines equal the units on disk; (b) docs/decisions.md starts with the exact bytes of its base version; (c) the CI athena-bin hashFiles globs and status::BUILD_PATHS cover each other, in both directions (this finds a real drift today: BUILD_PATHS lacks rust-toolchain.toml, athena.toml, defaults.toml and docs/system-facts.md, two of which the binary compiles in; the change adds them to BUILD_PATHS); (d) docs/ontology.toml terms against the governing docs, through ONE shared walk (scanned files, names, aliases, hits, uncovered lines) that moves from ontology.rs into mirrors.rs and is called by both ontology.rs and the registry. The before-handover call site is the producer loop's existing send-back (run/producer.rs), which already runs after every producer report and before verification on the one-commit snapshot. The registry runs there only for Athena's own source tree and only for entries whose mirror file exists. A drift is sent back with its message. The producer brief gets a short note, which is not the mechanism. A repo-level test target in athena-cli runs the registry over the real files and over a drifted fixture per entry, so a new entry is covered with no other edit.

decisions.choice: One registry REGISTRY: &[Mirror] with Mirror { name, mirror, source: Source, rule: Rule }. Source is Path | Glob | GitHead | Files; Rule is TimingUnits | AppendOnly | HashFilesCover(&'static [&'static str]) | OntologyTerms. check_entry(entry, root, base) and check_all(root, base) return Vec<Drift> (mirror, message naming the file and the fix). base: &dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> is injected. is_athena_source(root) (setup.sh, xtask/shard-timings.txt and crates/athena-core/Cargo.toml all exist) gates the producer-loop use, and an entry whose mirror file is absent is skipped.
decisions.reason: The cause is that nothing makes a mirror declare how it is compared to its source. A registry makes the declaration the unit, and the repo test iterates it. The gate keeps jobs on other repositories, which may have their own docs/decisions.md, from being forced to append-only.

rejected.option: One more one-off test per mirror, as the five jobs did
rejected.why: Fixes one instance and leaves the class.

rejected.option: Put the registry in xtask
rejected.why: xtask does not depend on athena-core, so it cannot read status::BUILD_PATHS, and xtask tests run in a heavy shard that is not part of the producer loop.

rejected.option: Run the registry on every repository the producer works in
rejected.why: docs/decisions.md append-only is Athena's own convention, so other repositories would get false send-backs.

decisions.choice: Rule (c) is two-way and the rule data is the compiled constant: Rule::HashFilesCover(&status::BUILD_PATHS). Mirror = crates/athena-core/src/status.rs, Source::Path(.github/workflows/ci.yml). hash_glob_problems(ci_text, build_paths) reads every line starting `key: athena-bin-`. (i) Each hashFiles glob must be covered by a BUILD_PATHS root (a root ending `/` covers a glob that starts with it, a file root covers its exact name); else the message says add the path to BUILD_PATHS in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs. (ii) Each root must be covered by a glob (a dir root needs a glob that starts with it and ends `**`); else the message says add the glob to every athena-bin key. A ci.yml with no such line is a drift. BUILD_PATHS becomes the nine roots crates/, xtask/, rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, athena.toml, defaults.toml, setup.sh, docs/system-facts.md, and stale_build_line prints the list from the constant. No excusals are needed.
decisions.reason: Critic finding 4. policy.rs (xtask/tests/policy.rs lines 783 and 897-1000) already proves the key equals xtask BUILD_INPUT_GLOBS (xtask/src/main.rs 267-277), the true input set. So the direction that can fail is: a glob in that key that BUILD_PATHS lacks. I read the code: athena.toml is compiled into non-test code (athena-gate lib.rs 33 BUILTIN_CONFIG), docs/system-facts.md too (athena-context briefs.rs 1671 SYSTEM_FACTS), and rust-toolchain.toml changes the compiler. touches_build (status.rs 23-29) and stale_build_line (35-58) ignore all of these, so a landing that changes them leaves a stale binary with no rebuild. That is a hand-kept list contradicting its source. defaults.toml is an xtask build input; adding it costs at most an extra rebuild and keeps one rule with no excusal list. Reading the constant directly means no parsing of status.rs and no second copy.

rejected.option: Only check that the key covers BUILD_PATHS (the previous plan)
rejected.why: True by construction, because policy.rs forces the key to be a superset; it can barely fail and misses the real drift.

rejected.option: Excuse the four extra globs with reasons and leave BUILD_PATHS alone
rejected.why: The files are compiled in, so the installed binary really is stale after a change to them; an excusal would keep the bug.

rejected.option: Re-derive the input set from include_str! scans
rejected.why: A weaker copy of what policy.rs proves.

rejected.option: Edit ci.yml
rejected.why: Governance, out of scope, and the key is already the true input set.

decisions.choice: Rule (d) shares the whole walk with ontology.rs. mirrors.rs gets plain-data types OntologyTerm { name, aliases, sources, senses: Vec<SenseRef{in_file, marker}>, excused: Vec<ExcuseRef{files, marker, reason}> } (Debug, Clone, PartialEq) and pub fns is_word_char, phrase_in, names_term, is_identifying, Hit, scan, is_decision_id, names_of, scanned_files(term, read_file), term_hits(term, read_file), excuse_ok(term, excuse) and uncovered_lines(term, hits) (the loop at ontology.rs 413-430, message text unchanged), plus parse_ontology(toml_text) -> Result<Vec<OntologyTerm>, String> using toml_edit, and ontology_problems(toml_text, read_file). read_file: &dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<String>; a source counts as a file when read_file returns Some. ontology.rs keeps its serde types and its sense/says and excuse-shape checks, converts each serde Term with a plain() fn, and calls the shared fns. A new test in ontology.rs, both_parsers_read_the_same_terms, asserts plain(serde term) == parse_ontology(text) term by term on the real file.
decisions.reason: Critic finding 5. Moving only the line matchers left the term walk and a second schema parser in mirrors.rs. athena-core has toml_edit but not toml (athena-core Cargo.toml lines 21-26), so the parser cannot be shared; the remaining difference is only the parse. The agreement test guards that difference on the real file, and the walk has one copy.

rejected.option: Re-implement the walk beside the original
rejected.why: A new hand-kept mirror of the ontology logic.

rejected.option: Add the toml crate to athena-core
rejected.why: Changes Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock for one parser; --locked builds make that a larger change.

rejected.option: Move all of claim_problems and the serde types into athena-core
rejected.why: A large refactor of a working test; the sense/says and excuse-shape checks are not part of the uncovered-line drift.

decisions.choice: Rule (a) derives `--test` and `--lib` units from disk: crates/*/tests/*.rs, crates/*/tests/*/main.rs and xtask/tests (unit `<dir name> --test <stem>`), and crates/*/src/lib.rs (unit `<dir name> --lib`). missing_timing_lines(units, timings_text) reports a unit missing from the file, and a `--test` or `--lib` line with no unit; `--doc` and `--bin` lines are never reported. A real-repo test, derived_units_agree_with_cargo_metadata, runs `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 --locked` (as xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs does around line 120) and asserts that the `--test` and `--lib` units of the targets with test=true equal the derived set. D158 states that `--doc` and `--bin` stay with the heavier oracle in ci_shards.rs (around line 420).
decisions.reason: Critic finding 7. A new crate's lib is as likely to be missed as a test file, and src/lib.rs is a cheap fact on disk. The agreement test makes the derived copy and the cargo-metadata original compared on the real repo. `--bin` names can be renamed (athena-cli's bin is `athena`), and `--doc` depends on the doctest flag, so deriving them from disk would be a guess; the limit is stated, not hidden.

rejected.option: Derive `--bin` and `--doc` units too
rejected.why: Needs Cargo.toml parsing for renamed bins and the doctest flag; it re-creates cargo metadata.

rejected.option: Name the ci_shards test as the rule and only run it
rejected.why: Criterion 3 needs a unit test that fails when a test file is missing; ci_shards runs in the heavy xtask lane and cannot be called with literal text.

rejected.option: Make xtask depend on athena-core
rejected.why: Changes xtask/Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock, and pulls a heavy crate into a CI-support crate.

decisions.choice: Rule (b) append_only_problem(base: &[u8], new: &[u8]) fails unless base is a byte prefix of new and names the first changed line and the fix (append, do not edit). The base comes from the injected closure. The producer loop builds it from `snapshot.git().show_file(snapshot.base(), path)` (athena-git lib.rs 453, snapshot.rs 122 and 131). The repo test uses `git_base(root)` with HEAD. A None base skips the rule.
decisions.reason: This is the rag3 prevention. The producer's snapshot is a git repository whose base commit is the dispatch base, so the base text is in the snapshot while it edits. crates/athena-cli/src/decisions.rs keeps its PINNED_LEN/PINNED_SHA256 test for committed history.

rejected.option: Replace the pinned-hash test
rejected.why: It guards committed history, which a base comparison cannot.

rejected.option: Compare with origin/main
rejected.why: The snapshot has no remote.

decisions.choice: The before-handover call site is the producer loop's existing self-check in crates/athena-core/src/run/producer.rs (after unmet/unchanged/gate/outside, lines 285-320). Add `let mirrors = if self.nested.is_none() && !changes.is_empty() { mirror_drift_in(&snapshot) } else { Vec::new() };`, add `&& mirrors.is_empty()` to the break condition, push `files kept by hand disagree with their source: ...` into `problems` after the `report_problems` clone (like the gate, so the verifier is not told the report lacked it), and append the messages to the send-back brief with a new pure fn append_mirror_drift(text, drift) in run/send_back.rs that returns the text unchanged for an empty list. mirror_drift_in returns an empty list unless mirrors::is_athena_source(snapshot.dir()). It shares the one PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS slot; a drift still present at the limit leaves the loop with a ui line, and the configured `cargo test --locked` check (which runs athena-cli --test mirrors) is the backstop. A nested run is judged by the outer job.
decisions.reason: Critic finding 6. The mechanism the 'mechanism' default and criterion 5 ask for is an invocation, not a sentence. The loop already runs before verification on the one-commit snapshot, so git_base works, and its tests (run/tests.rs fake-agent harness, governed_job_with and editing) show how to demonstrate it. A hook in run_check was rightly dropped earlier (it runs after handover and can be excused by is_pre_existing at verify.rs line 203).

rejected.option: A producer-brief instruction only (the previous plan)
rejected.why: Prose a producer can skip.

rejected.option: A hook in checks.rs run_check or a new CheckKind
rejected.why: Runs after handover in the verifier's snapshot, can be masked by the pre-existing excuse, and a CheckKind changes the governance config schema.

rejected.option: Add a new argument to every send_back_text_* variant
rejected.why: Touches four functions and their tests for one list; a wrapper that appends a section leaves them unchanged.

decisions.choice: Keep a short producer-brief note, MIRROR_CHECK_INSTRUCTION, in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs, built like BOUNDARY_SCAN_INSTRUCTION (line 787): run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors` before finishing; it names the file and the fix. It is written by mirror_check_section() and pushed in producer_brief_with_evidence between the banned-words section and `## Checks Athena will run`. It is marked as a helper in D158, not the mechanism.
decisions.reason: Critic finding 6 says the line can stay. It lets the producer fix drift in its own loop instead of using the one send-back. The briefs sit outside the budget sets (system-facts 'Prompt sets and budgets'), so no budget line changes.

rejected.option: Drop the brief note
rejected.why: Costs the producer its one send-back for an avoidable drift.

risks.risk: Changing BUILD_PATHS makes a landing that touches athena.toml, defaults.toml, rust-toolchain.toml or docs/system-facts.md trigger a rebuild in the drain, and a drain test that landed athena.toml (tests/drain.rs line 3117) may assert no rebuild.
risks.mitigation: This is the intended fix, since the first two are compiled into the binary or change the compiler. The producer runs `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` and changes only an expectation that asserted no rebuild, saying so in the report.

risks.risk: The loop hook sends back on a false positive in the real tree, for example a mirror that already drifts at the base, so the producer cannot fix it.
risks.mitigation: The real-repo test runs at base in step 5 and any drift there is fixed or the rule corrected before the loop test is written. The loop only sends back once and then leaves the loop with a ui line. The configured test check is the backstop.

risks.risk: The registry runs on a repository that is not Athena's source and fails it.
risks.mitigation: is_athena_source gate, plus skip when a mirror file is absent. A loop test uses a repository without those files and asserts no send-back.

risks.risk: Moving the ontology walk changes ontology.rs behavior, or the two parsers diverge.
risks.mitigation: Functions move verbatim, with is_word_char alphanumeric only and the messages unchanged. The existing ontology tests run, and both_parsers_read_the_same_terms compares the plain data of both parsers on the real file.

risks.risk: Derived `--test` and `--lib` units diverge from cargo's target set, for example a [[test]] with a custom path.
risks.mitigation: derived_units_agree_with_cargo_metadata on the real repo; on disagreement the producer fixes the derivation, not the timings file.

risks.risk: The append-only rule compares with the base, so it is trivially true once committed and skipped with no git.
risks.mitigation: It bites on uncommitted edits, which is the producer's loop. The decisions.rs pin still guards committed history. D158 states the limit.

risks.risk: The drift shares the single send-back slot, so a producer already sent back for unmet criteria gets no second chance for drift.
risks.mitigation: Same as the gate today. The drift then stays and the configured `cargo test --locked` fails on athena-cli --test mirrors, so it is caught at verification, as before. D158 states this.

risks.risk: A future mirror is added but never registered, so the class returns.
risks.mitigation: The module doc and D158 say the registry is where a mirror is declared, and mark registration prose-only. A new Rule variant without a fixture fails to compile in the repo test.

risks.risk: The producer's 'Planned files left unchanged' check flags checks.rs, which the reading lists.
risks.mitigation: The report explains it is unchanged because the hook moved to the producer loop (the last decision).

risks.risk: The shard-timings value for the new target is a guess.
risks.mitigation: The file header says values are estimates and the cover test checks names only; use 6.00, near the ontology target.

demonstrations.method: Read the change description in its homes: the `//!` doc of mirrors.rs, the CHANGELOG.md bullet under [Unreleased] / Added, and the appended D158. Each names the root cause in the same words: hand-kept mirrors of a governing source are tested for structure only, not content against the source, and the registry is the fix.
demonstrations.observes: The diff for CHANGELOG.md and docs/decisions.md shows only added lines. D158 follows D157 and has Case, Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost and Provenance. It names the root cause, the four rules and the reversed BUILD_PATHS rule, and says which parts are prose only (the brief note, registering a new mirror). It states the limits: the HEAD comparison is trivial once committed, `--doc` and `--bin` units stay with ci_shards, and decisions.rs PINNED_* and xtask BUILD_INPUT_GLOBS remain separate pins. It justifies the shard-timings line and the checks.rs omission. status.rs shows nine BUILD_PATHS roots.

demonstrations.method: Read mirrors.rs and lib.rs. REGISTRY holds four entries, each with a mirror path, a described Source and a Rule. `pub mod mirrors;` is in lib.rs with a line in the module list.
demonstrations.observes: crates/athena-core/src/mirrors.rs is new; lib.rs, ontology.rs, run/producer.rs, run/send_back.rs, run/tests.rs, status.rs, tests/drain.rs, tests/mirrors.rs, briefs.rs, shard-timings.txt, CHANGELOG.md and decisions.md are listed; checks.rs is not. Grep for `REGISTRY` and `pub mod mirrors` in the two files shows the four entries and the export.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in mirrors::tests and in run::tests (names beginning `mirrors_`), each rule with a failing and a passing case, calling the pure rule fns with literal text. missing_timing_lines: a test file absent from the timings fails and names xtask/shard-timings.txt and `add the line`; a stale `--test` line fails; a `--doc`, `--bin` or other-package line is not reported. append_only_problem: a rewritten decision line fails and names docs/decisions.md and the first changed line; added text passes. hash_glob_problems: a ci text whose key hashes `athena.toml` while the roots lack it fails with `add ... to BUILD_PATHS in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs`; a roots list with `setup.sh` removed from the key fails with `add the glob`; a dir root with only `crates/` and no `**` fails; no athena-bin key fails; a matching pair passes. uncovered_lines and ontology_problems: a governing-doc line `Hermes: a role ...` for a term with only a tool sense fails and names docs/ontology.toml and `add a senses entry`; a covering sense or a valid excuse passes. check_all over a tempfile tree with a closure for base: the clean tree gives no drift, a None base skips rule (b), and a tree that is not an Athena source gives none. Also in run::tests, with the fake-agent harness (see seam): the producer adds crates/demo/tests/b.rs and no timings line, so the second producer prompt carries `## Sent back`, `xtask/shard-timings.txt` and `add the line`, and the job is sent back once; a producer that adds the timings line on the send-back reaches the verifier; a clean producer is not sent back; a repository that is not Athena's source is not sent back.
demonstrations.observes: All tests pass. Each negative case returns a non-empty Vec whose text names the offending file and the fix. The loop tests count producer runs 2 and verifier runs 1 for the fixed case, and producer runs 1 with no `## Sent back` for the clean and non-Athena cases.
demonstrations.fails_without: Before the change the module does not exist, so no test matches. Without a rule, the pure test for that rule gets an empty Vec and its non-empty assertion fails. Without the producer-loop call, the second producer prompt has no `## Sent back` and the verifier runs with the drift in place, so the send-back test fails. Without the is_athena_source gate, the non-Athena test fails. Without the BUILD_PATHS fix, the hashFiles case against the real constant (asserted in the athena-cli real-repo test) fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: mirrors::missing_timing_lines, append_only_problem, hash_glob_problems, uncovered_lines, ontology_problems, check_all, and Athena::go through producer_loop in run/producer.rs. Doubles: literal strings, a tempfile tree (tempfile is an athena-core dependency, Cargo.toml line 24), a closure for base that returns fixed bytes and has no comparison logic, and the fake agent script. The script is built with the existing helpers in run/tests.rs: repo(), commit_file(), governed_job_with(repo, script) and editing(counts, prompts, extra_edits), which add extra file edits to the producer turn and record prompts (all exist, read at run/tests.rs lines 2206-2271). The mirrors module and the pure fns are added by plan steps 2-4. The loop call, append_mirror_drift and the fixture tests are added by step 6.

demonstrations.method: New test target crates/athena-cli/tests/mirrors.rs with four tests. (1) the_real_repo_has_no_mirror_drift calls check_all(repo_root, git_base(repo_root)) and prints every Drift. (2) every_registry_entry_catches_its_drifted_fixture iterates REGISTRY. For each entry it builds a tempdir fixture with an exhaustive `match entry.rule` (a new Rule variant without a fixture fails to compile), drifts it one way and asserts check_entry returns a Drift naming entry.mirror and the fix, and also asserts a clean fixture gives none. A new entry with an existing Rule is covered with no other edit. (3) derived_units_agree_with_cargo_metadata compares mirrors::test_units(root) with the `--test` and `--lib` units from cargo metadata (serde_json is an athena-cli dependency). (4) the_ci_key_and_build_paths_cover_each_other runs hash_glob_problems on the real ci.yml and status::BUILD_PATHS. Also run the ontology target to prove the shared walk and both parsers agree: both_parsers_read_the_same_terms and the existing the_ontology_file_is_sound.
demonstrations.observes: All pass. Then `cargo test -p athena-cli --test ontology` passes. A producer who adds a test file without a timings line, rewrites an old decision, edits ci.yml or BUILD_PATHS in one place only, or leaves an uncovered ontology line sees test (1) fail with the file and the fix.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the registry the target does not compile. With a stubbed rule, test (2) fails for that entry. Without the xtask/shard-timings.txt line `athena-cli --test mirrors`, test (1) names that file. With BUILD_PATHS left at five roots, tests (1) and (4) fail on `athena.toml`. If derivation diverges from cargo metadata, test (3) fails. If the ontology parsers differ, both_parsers_read_the_same_terms fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: mirrors::check_all, check_entry, git_base, REGISTRY, test_units, hash_glob_problems, parse_ontology. Root is Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../..") (pattern at ontology.rs line 90). Fixtures: tempfile trees; check_entry takes a fixed base closure. athena-cli has athena-core, tempfile and serde_json already. The target and its fixtures are added by plan step 5, and the functions by steps 2-4. Cargo.lock does not change.

They cover the new athena-cli mirrors target, the loop tests, the moved ontology walk, the changed BUILD_PATHS (athena-cli tests/drain.rs touches_build and stale-line tests, athena-core status tests), xtask ci_shards (timings cover) and the existing decisions pin.
